title: What Plants Need to Grow
keyIdea: A plant needs water, light and warmth to grow and stay well. With no water it dries up and flops. In the dark it goes pale and weak. In the cold it hardly grows. Too much water is bad too, because the roots sit in water.
familyTip: Plant three cress pots on the same day. Keep one on a sunny windowsill with water, one in a dark cupboard with water, and one on the windowsill with no water. Look every day for a week and draw what you see.

visual.caption: Will the plant grow well? Drag each card into a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: sitting in a puddle of water

lab.caption: Flagship lab: grow two pots for a week with and without water, light or warmth, try too much water, make a fair test and help a sad plant.

kid: Plants are alive. They need things to grow, just like you. A plant needs water, light and warmth.
Give a plant no water and it gets dry. Its leaves flop down. Put it in a dark cupboard and it goes pale and thin. It may grow tall, but it is weak.
Put a plant in the fridge and it hardly grows at all. It is too cold. A warm room is just right.
Too much water is bad too. If the pot sits in a puddle, the roots get sick. Give a plant some water, not a flood.
adult: Ages 6 to 8. This is the Year 2 Plants requirement in England: find out and describe how plants need water, light and a suitable temperature to grow and stay healthy. It matches NGSS 2-LS2-1, planning an investigation into whether plants need sunlight and water. It follows Growing from a seed and comes before the Year 3 work on what each plant part does.

Green plants make their own food from light, water and carbon dioxide, so a plant kept in the dark uses up its store. It grows long and pale, a change called etiolation, and then fails. Cold slows growth because the plant's chemistry runs slowly. Waterlogged soil leaves roots short of air, so leaves yellow and wilt. The plant sizes in the lab are a simple model, not measurements.

Common mistakes: thinking plants get their food from the soil, or that soil alone is enough. Thinking more water is always better. Reading the tall plant in the dark as the healthiest one. And running an unfair test, such as moving one pot into the dark and also stopping its water.

In the lab your child grows two pots side by side for a week, changing one thing each time: water, light or warmth. They try no water, some water and too much. Then they set up a fair test for light and help a sad plant by giving it water, light and warmth.

choices: one in a dark cupboard, watered
one on a sunny windowsill, watered
one on a sunny windowsill, not watered
practice.hint: A plant needs water, light and warmth.
practice.explain: The windowsill plant with water has light, water and warmth, so it grows best. The others are missing light or water.

practice.prompt: A plant was left in a dark cupboard for a week. It is tall, thin and pale. Is it healthy?
choices: no, it is weak because it had no light
practice.hint: Look at the colour, not just the height.
practice.explain: In the dark a plant cannot make its food. It stretches up looking for light, but it is pale and weak, not healthy.

practice.prompt: A bean plant on the windowsill is {a} cm tall. A bean plant kept in the fridge is {b} cm tall. How many cm taller is the windowsill plant?
practice.hint: Take the fridge plant's height away from the windowsill plant's height.
practice.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b} cm. The fridge was too cold, so that plant hardly grew.

practice.prompt: Sam's plant grows {a} cm each week on a warm windowsill. How tall will it grow in 2 weeks, in cm?
practice.hint: Add the growth for week 1 and week 2.
practice.explain: {a} + {a} = {=2*a} cm. With water, light and warmth every week, it keeps growing.

practice.prompt: Ava wants to test if plants need light. Pot B goes in the dark. What should she keep the same?
practice.hint: A fair test changes only one thing.
practice.explain: Only the light should change. If the water or warmth changes too, Ava cannot tell what made the difference.

pool.prompt: What three things does a plant need to grow well?
pool.hint: Think of the three things you changed in the lab.
pool.explain: Plants need water, light and a warm enough place. Soil helps hold the plant up, but it is not enough on its own.

pool.prompt: Leo forgot to water his plant for two weeks. What will it look like?
pool.hint: What happened to pot B in the lab with no water?
pool.explain: Without water the plant dries out. Its leaves droop and can turn brown.

pool.prompt: Why is it bad to leave a plant pot standing in a puddle of water every day?
choices: too much water hurts the roots
the water makes it grow too fast
pool.hint: Roots need some air as well as water.
pool.explain: Roots sitting in water get no air, so they get sick. The leaves turn yellow and droop.

pool.prompt: A plant is kept in the fridge with water and a light. What happens?
pool.hint: Is the fridge warm or cold?
pool.explain: The fridge is too cold for the plant to grow well, so it hardly grows.

pool.prompt: Two pots are the same, but one is in a dark box and gets no water. Why is this not a fair test?
choices: two things changed: light and water
pool.hint: Count how many things are different.
pool.explain: Light and water both changed, so you cannot tell which one made the plant weak. Change only one thing.

pool.prompt: A sad plant is pale and floppy. It was in a cold, dark corner with no water. What should you do?
choices: give it water and move it somewhere warm and light
pool.explain: It was missing water, light and warmth. Give it all three and it can grow again.

pool.prompt: A cress pot in the light grew {a} cm. A cress pot in the dark grew {b} cm taller, but it was pale and weak. How tall did the dark pot grow, in cm?
pool.hint: Add the extra height to the first height.
pool.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b} cm. Taller is not healthier: without light the cress is pale and floppy.

pool.prompt: You plant {a} seeds on a warm, sunny windowsill and water them. {b} of them do not grow. How many grow?
pool.hint: Take away the ones that did not grow.
pool.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b} seeds grow. Even with water, light and warmth, a few seeds may not grow.
